scenario_description:
Objective: Keep a family indigo rebozo from being damaged while a textile memory-circle plan becomes definite.
Emerging Need: A general invitation becomes relevant after the borrowed rebozo is named, then venue display instructions introduce clipping and direct sun before an adjustment cutoff.
Decision Context: Messages and venue notices establish the item’s movement, display method, access limits, and deadline; stored care notes supply the hidden handling boundary.
Consequence: A shaded-table arrangement or withholding display can prevent the rebozo’s first clipped, sunlit exposure. After mounting and the welcome photo, that initial exposure cannot be undone; prompt removal can still limit further harm.

parameter.subject: Saturday textile memory circle: bring-or-browse welcome
parameter.body: Millefleur Folk Arts Center will host a small textile memory circle on Saturday, March 14. Guests may bring a personal cloth to discuss or may simply listen. Depending on the weather, the circle may use both the indoor side room and the courtyard. Final setup details will follow later in the week.

parameter.title: Textile memory circle at Millefleur
parameter.description: Small bring-or-browse textile conversation; venue setup details pending.
parameter.location: Millefleur Folk Arts Center, Santa Fe

parameter.content: I found the cedar sleeve with your indigo rebozo while clearing my guest-room bench. I’m going to carry it with me Saturday so it can come back to you after the textile circle; it might be a lovely example if the conversation turns that way.

parameter.subject: Textile circle setup: courtyard rail labels and shade requests
parameter.body: For Saturday’s memory circle, brought textiles for the share table will be intake-labeled, then clipped with padded clothespins to the south courtyard rail for the 1:45 welcome photo and first discussion pass. The rail gets direct sun after lunch. Anyone needing a shaded table placement instead should reply by Friday, March 13 at 5:00 PM, before the layout cards are printed.

parameter.content: I dropped the cedar sleeve at Millefleur’s early intake desk on my way to the frame shop. The volunteer said the layout cards printed at five, the display room is locked for the evening, and textile pickups or placement changes wait until doors open tomorrow just before mounting starts.

The welcome photo has just been taken. Your indigo rebozo is clipped to the south courtyard rail in direct sun with the other cloths. I can see indentations where the padded clips grip it. The doors are open now and I am beside the display.
